section_1.title: The Architecture: Guessing and Checking
section_1.content: Introduce the neural network as a series of connected 'nodes' that transform input data into a prediction. Define the 'Loss Function' as the measure of how wrong the network is.
section_1.example: A robot trying to identify a picture of a cat vs. a dog. If it labels a cat as a 'dog', the 'Loss' is the distance between the wrong guess and the ground truth.

section_2.title: The Mechanism: Credit Assignment Problem
section_2.content: Explain that each node has a 'weight' (importance). When the network makes an error, we need to know: which weights contributed most to this mistake? This is the prerequisite for understanding Backpropagation.
section_2.example: Imagine a relay race team where the team loses. Backpropagation is the coach walking backward from the finish line to identify which runner was too slow.

section_3.title: The Core: Intuitive Backpropagation (The Chain Rule)
section_3.content: Visualize the network as a chain of gears. Backpropagation propagates the error gradient from the output layer back to the input layer using the calculus 'Chain Rule'. Keep it visual: the error 'flows' backward like water through a pipe.
section_3.example: Use a graphical animation: A glowing red 'Error' dot travels backward through the layers, leaving behind 'update signals' that tell each weight how to adjust itself to reduce the error.

section_4.title: The Update: Gradient Descent
section_4.content: Explain that after calculating the 'blame' for each weight, we perform a tiny step to adjust them. Emphasize that we do this thousands of times until the error is minimized.
section_4.example: Represent this as a hiker (the network) walking down a foggy mountain (the error landscape) using only the slope under their feet (gradient) to find the valley floor.

section_5.title: Conclusion: From Noise to Wisdom
section_5.content: Summarize that learning is essentially the repeated cycle of Forward Pass (prediction) and Backward Pass (correction).
section_5.example: Show the robot from Section 1 evolving: initially, it guesses randomly; after thousands of backpropagation steps, it identifies a cat with 99% accuracy.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=GRAY) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 1.0 + j * 1.2

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
